_readme: The PF1e weapon-size damage conversion. Hand-authored from the printed table rather than scraped -- weapons_data.json carries only 'damage: 1d4 (small), 1d6 (medium)' and there is no size-progression table anywhere else in the backend. Gated by Backend/scripts/gates/validate_gear_legality.py, which checks the shape, the ladder and the one-step-up consistency; the VALUES are external rules and their authority is the sources named below, not this repo.
source: Pathfinder RPG Core Rulebook, Table 6-5: Tiny and Large Weapon Damage. Transcribed 2026-08-17 and verified row-for-row against two independent copies -- aonprd.com/Rules.aspx?ID=110 and roll20.net/compendium/pathfinder/Weapons -- which agree exactly.
attack_penalty_rule: A creature can't make optimum use of a weapon that isn't properly sized for it. A cumulative -2 penalty applies on attack rolls for each size category of difference. (Core Rulebook, quoted verbatim.)

steps_published.note: The Core Rulebook publishes exactly two conversions off the Medium value: Tiny (two steps down) and Large (one step up). Small and Medium are printed per-weapon in the weapon tables themselves, which is what weapons_data.json's 'NdX (small), NdY (medium)' already carries. There is NO published Huge-or-larger weapon damage table in PF1e -- see 'gap' below.

gap.what: A MEDIUM-sized character oversized by TWO steps (Medium -> Huge) cannot be resolved from this file, because PF1e never published a Huge weapon damage table. Applying the Large column twice does not work either: it has no row for 3d6, 3d8, 4d6 or 4d8.
gap.who_hits_it: Only the full Titan Slayer chain (Power Attack + Titan Technique + Titan Grip + Titan Slayer, Str 19, BAB +8) reaches +2, and per ruling D10 the generator never GRANTS its way there -- +2 requires a character who already holds the whole chain.
gap.not_hit_by: A SMALL character at +1 or +2 is fully covered without this table: +1 is the weapon's own printed medium damage, and +2 is the 'large' column here.
gap.rejected: The community 'Medium and Larger Weapon Damage' table that continues into Huge/Gargantuan/Colossal is NOT transcribed here. It could not be verified against a first-party source in the same pass as Table 6-5, and the Paizo FAQ damage-dice progression chart -- the other candidate -- deliberately disagrees with Table 6-5 (it steps 1d8 to 1d10 and 2d6 to 2d8, where the weapon-size table steps them to 2d6 and 3d6). Guessing which one applies to a physically larger weapon would put an unsourced rule in a file whose whole job is to be the source.
gap.until_then: Consumers must cap a Medium wielder at +1 step and say so, rather than silently returning the unchanged dice.
